text: Riverton (Synthetic News) -- Officials in District 1 faced a crowded hearing on January 12 after the transport authority released a plan covering a delayed bridge inspection program. Mayor Elena Ruiz said the proposal would begin with a $4 million pilot and expand only if outside reviewers confirm that early targets are met. The plan follows months of complaints from residents who said earlier notices were confusing and that service changes arrived with little warning. Under the current schedule, department staff will publish cost estimates, hold two neighborhood sessions, and report participation numbers within 30 days. Residents welcomed the added oversight but asked for clearer deadlines. Several council members asked whether smaller towns would receive the same level of attention as the central business district. Officials said the first public dashboard will include spending, complaint response times, and a plain-language explanation of any delays. No final vote is expected until staff compare the pilot results with baseline data gathered last year.
